## Checking soil suitability data is stored and pretty clean
- it is stored, however there are a few columns that appear redundant and/or unused
```{python}
data_dir= Path("Data")
path = data_dir / "soil-suitability" / "ACRPC_Soil_Septic.fgb"
df = pyogrio.read_dataframe(path)
df = crs_set(df)

display(df.head())
print(f'The number of rows is: {len(df)}')
```

and for the other geojson.

Notes about this wwtf geojson
- a lot of the columns seem redundant and like they should not be in there
- data does not line up with the wastewater treatment parquet
- the same issues are present in the above wastewater geojson as well
```{python}
path = data_dir / "wastewater" / "VermontWWTF.geojson"
df = gpd.read_file(path)
df = crs_set(df)

display(df.head())
print(f'The number of rows is: {len(df)}')
```


### Now doing this with the parquet file to see that things line up
note: this is different from the geojsons, they look much cleaner
```{python}
path = data_dir / "wastewater" / "ww_treatment_facilities.parquet"
df = gpd.read_parquet(path)
df = crs_set(df)

display(df.head())
print(f'The number of rows is: {len(df)}')
```
